findings.issue: Used `pkill -f "node src/index.js"` in a way that killed its own shell's process group (exit 143), then repeated the identical mistake at cleanup (trace.md:985)
findings.suggestion: Start servers with a captured PID (`echo $! > /tmp/app.pid`) and kill by PID, or use setsid/nohup disassociation consistently

findings.issue: Debug repro script written to /tmp, where Node ESM resolution couldn't find the playwright package, costing a failed call
findings.suggestion: Write repro scripts inside the repo (or import from '@playwright/test' with cwd at repo root from the start), as it did on the retry

findings.issue: Attempted an edit against code it misremembered from a long thinking block; the bug didn't exist
findings.suggestion: Re-read the target lines before editing after an extended reasoning gap instead of trusting recall

summary: A near-exemplary session: exhaustive reconnaissance (spec, tests, data shapes, all 10 reference screenshots) before a single write, then one clean implementation pass with only two real bugs, each diagnosed from evidence and fixed in one edit. Verification went beyond the test suite — curl-probed edge cases, sanity-checked hono/html semantics, and compared its own desktop and mobile screenshots page-by-page against the references, with a full suite re-run after the last edit. The only waste was ~6 turns: a repeated pkill-kills-own-shell mistake, a misplaced repro script, and a phantom-bug edit miss, none of which derailed progress.
